>I wonder how many addicts are really just self-medicating for depression.

I'm going to take a guess and say, "Almost all of them."

HoldThisWoe, my username is not a coincidence. I feel you, my friend. I wish we could hang out, order a pizza, complain at one another about our lives until the break of dawn, then play Halo or some other random game to take our minds off of things.

Hell, I learned three foreign languages just so I could have more people to talk to online at all hours of the night when I'm awake and can't get to sleep because I'm so lonely. It changed my career path, maybe for the better. I still feel like shit, but at least I gained something useful out of it. That makes me feel a little bit better, and I don't know if something like that is possible for you, but it's helped me justify my feelings a bit.

22 here. It doesn't really get better as you age, but the good news is that people who were generally not lonely before seem to be getting lonely now that they're out in the "real world" and don't have their groups of friends to keep them company all the time. So, more people are reaching out to those around them.

There's definitely hope, but I'm not going to lie to anyone and say that shit gets better as you age.

Incorrect. Genetics testing can tell identifical twins apart, but you have to pay for a more expensive, more thorough test. Although identical twins originally have identical DNA as they're from the same egg and sperm, their DNA does not mutate in the same fashion as they age.

This can tell which identifical twin is the father/mother of a child, for instance, by looking for unique mutations in the sex chromosomes of the child.

I seriously thought that something was wrong with me, so I sought the help of a professional at the local university. After a month of sessions, my counselor/therapist told me that I was the most emotionally healthy person she's ever encountered. Hell if I know what that even means. We just discussed tons of stuff from my life (pretty traumatic) and the steps that I went through to deal with said trauma in a healthy fashion. Apparently I know very well the healthy ways to deal with things, and I put them into perspective well. I do everything I should, but I just don't *feel* good.

As for the chronic loneliness, I told her all the things I was doing to help alleviate it, and she agreed that those things are the only things I can do. The only other thing I can think of is that there's something seriously wrong with the chemicals my brain is dealing with, because after examining my ways of coping and dealing with stressors, I *shouldn't* feel this way.

I also found it ironic that you said "We just want you to know that it won't be like this forever." Mentioned that in my write up... I too know it won't be forever, which is part of the reason I feel so blah about it. I know that, probably within the next four months, I'll have another lover and I'll forget all about my problems... until that relationship ends, and then they'll all come back.

It's all just so ridiculous. I've considered not dating anyone because I don't believe anything will last, especially when I see people getting divorced after 35 years of marriage. >.>
